sentences: Blepharitis is a common inflammatory disease of the eyelid margins characterized by chronic inflammation, scaling, and crusting, which may also cause swelling, burning, itching, or a grainy sensation when introducing foreign objects or substances to the eye

It can affect any age group and is often associated with various systemic diseases, particularly rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis, as well as other ocular conditions like dry eye, chalazion, conjunctivitis, and keratitis
Blepharitis can be classified into two main types: anterior and posterior, based on the location of the inflammation, and into acute and chronic types, based on the duration of symptoms

The exact pathogenesis of blepharitis is not fully understood, but it is thought to be caused by bacterial colonization (Staphylococcus aureus or Staphylococcus epidermidis) in the eyelids or meibomian gland dysfunction, as well as by allergens and lice that affect the eyelashes
Other causes of blepharitis include Demodex folliculorum, a small parasitic mite
Common symptoms associated with blepharitis include burning sensation, irritation, tearing, photophobia, blurred vision, and red eyes

Clinical examination reveals scurf, telangiectatic vascular changes of the eyelid margin, inspissated meibomian glands, conjunctival hyperemia, punctuate keratopathy, cornea vascularization, and ulceration

Blepharitis is diagnosed based on clinical features alone and is managed with eyelid hygiene and regular cleaning, along with antimicrobial topical therapy in some cases, depending on the causative pathogen and underlying cause
There are various forms of blepharitis, including seborrheic, staphylococcal, mixed, posterior or meibomitis, or parasitic, and it affects all ages and ethnic groups
